nodes.question: What issues arise due to the inconsistencies between different databases used in LCA?
nodes.answer: Inconsistencies between databases can create problems of comparability between the different analyses performed.

As the The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment environmental impacts of industrial activities evolve rapidly over time, the availability of up-to-date data is crucial for conducting LCA that reflects real changes (Teh et al. 2020; Carri res et al. 2021). Furthermore, databases often appear inconsistent with each other due to different development approaches, thus raising problems of comparability between the different analyses performed (Zhang et al. 2020; Sica et al. 2022). In this framework, the use of digital technologies (DTs) is emerging as a valuable solution to improve the Life Cycle Inventory phase (Ingrao et al. 2021; Sica et al. 2022; Yang et al. 2023; Chen et al. 2024). They include tools such as cloud computing, blockchain, big data analytics, and simulation (Bai et al. 2020 ). nodes.question: How is NEMO valuable for ecological impact modelling in the transport sector?
nodes.answer: NEMO is valuable for ecological impact modelling in the transport sector as it is used for the mandatory annual compilation of the official Austrian air pollutant and greenhouse gas inventory, allowing for the assessment of transport emissions resulting from different measures and ambition levels up to 2050.

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What specific type of analysis was implemented to explore the impact of biogenic carbon in the study?
nodes.answer: A dynamic life cycle impact assessment (LCIA) was performed to analyze both short- and long-term emissions including the impact of biogenic carbon.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Purpose Bio-based insulation materials can have a significant impact in achieving net zero target in the construction sector. However, they face challenges due to lack of data on environmental performances and professional perception, hindering their proliferation. This study aims to combine scenario-based and dynamic analyses of environmental performances to provide comprehensive environmental information on bio-based thermal insulation materials. The goal is to empower professionals with robust information, facilitating informed decisions and promoting the selection of bio-based materials. Methods Data on manufacturing, use, recyclability, and technical performance of eleven commercially available natural insulation materials were collected from the literature to create a Life Cycle Inventory (LCI). For each material, a scenario- based life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted by modelling variation in manufacturing, transportation, end-of-life and material properties, using the UK as the primary case study. Materials were compared to three non-bio-based insulation materials by ranking the thirteen environmental impact categories in EN 15804(2013) + A2(2019) to give an exhaustive overview of their potential benefits and burdens. Additionally, a dynamic LCIA was performed to implement in the analysis both short-and long-term emissions, exploring the impact of biogenic carbon.

nodes.question: What limitation is noted regarding the work of Schulte et al. (2021)?
nodes.answer: Schulte et al. (2021) is limited to a point-value result based on a single scenario for transportation, end-of-life, and material properties.

Nonetheless, also in this case prod- ucts with singularly defined technical performances were investigated. nodes.question: How does the lack of complete and quality data impact the LCA methodology?
nodes.answer: The lack of complete and quality data impacts the LCA methodology by affecting the Life Cycle Inventory phase, leading to potential inaccuracies and increased variability and uncertainty in the assessment results.
nodes.paragraph: However, the LCA methodology presents relevant chal- lenges that may affect its application in business contexts (Testa et al. 2016; Sassanelli et al. 2019) and in circular practices (Toniolo et al. 2023). These include the difficulty of collecting reliable and accurate data needed to ensure traceability and transparency of the analysis (Saberi et al. 2019; Sassanelli et al. 2019; Carri res et al. 2021). The lack of complete and quality data especially affects the Life Cycle Inventory phase (Notarnicola et al. 2022), which requires systematic collection of all inputs and outputs involved in the different stages of the product life cycle. Hence, the need to use estimates or exclude several steps in the pro- duction process, compromising the accuracy of assessments and increasing the variability and uncertainty of results (Salomone et al. 2010; Guo and Murphy 2012; Henriksen et al. 2019). nodes.answer: The life cycle stages included in the system boundary were transportation and production. nodes.question: What has become the de facto gold standard for quantifying environmental footprints of agri-food commodity supply chains?
nodes.answer: Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) has become the de facto gold standard for quantifying environmental footprints of agri-food commodity supply chains.
nodes.paragraph: The sophistication of LCA has evolved rapidly in recent years (e.g. McLaren et al. 2021) and arguably has become the de facto gold standard means to quantify environmental footprints of agri-food commodity supply chains in silico over the last few decades (lgos et al. 2019 ). Indeed, one such example of advancing LCA is how high-resolution data can catapult the method through the development of a novel approach to life cycle inventory analysis (LCI) by calculating GHG emissions of individual finishing cattle thus enabling the assessment of dependent (emissions) and independent variables (e.g. growth rates, breeds, and sex) to identify the most promising areas in terms of livestock management and GHG mitigation. Here, McAuliffe et al. (2018) found that average daily weight gains (ADG) were strongly (and negatively) correlated variables to individual animal carbon footprints, and that using averaged livestock performance data may underestimate emission intensities due to insufficient consideration being given to poorly per - forming animals, whose emissions become exponentially greater as their ADG decreases.
